levels.name: Kitchen table
levels.blurb: Paper, balloons, flour and sunlight: the physics of rockets and planets with things you already own.

levels.name: Garage & backyard
levels.blurb: Pressurised water rockets, a DVD spectroscope, cosmic-ray tracks and the turning sky, plus your first CAD.

levels.name: First real rockets
levels.blurb: Certified model-rocket motors, Barrowman stability, 3D-printed airframes and a flight recorder you program.

levels.name: Avionics & tracking
levels.blurb: Design a flight-computer circuit board, radio telemetry to a ground station, and a star tracker.

levels.name: Research grade
levels.blurb: High-power certification, validated simulation, near space, the hydrogen line and exoplanets.

experiments.title: Stomp rocket
experiments.summary: A paper rocket launched by stomping on a 2 L bottle. Feel impulse, then measure your apogee with an inclinometer and trigonometry.
experiments.safety: Eye protection; nobody in front of the launch tube.

experiments.title: Balloon rocket: Newton's third law
experiments.summary: A balloon on a string track. Film it in slow motion and plot speed against balloon volume to test momentum conservation.

experiments.title: Film-canister rocket
experiments.summary: Effervescent tablets make CO₂ until the lid pops. Stoichiometry, the ideal gas law, reaction rate vs temperature, and h = g t² / 8.
experiments.safety: Outdoors, eye protection, inside-snap lids only.

experiments.title: Pinhole Sun & sunspots
experiments.summary: Project the Sun through a pinhole, then a masked mirror onto a far wall. Track sunspots for a week and measure the Sun's rotation.
experiments.safety: Never look at the Sun; view the projection only.

experiments.title: Impact craters
experiments.summary: Drop balls into flour dusted with cocoa to make rayed craters, then fit a log–log power law: crater size grows as energy to the ¼.

experiments.title: Water bottle rocket
experiments.summary: PVC pull-string launcher, pressure gauge and an OpenSCAD nose cone + fin can for a 2 L bottle. A simulator finds the best water fill.
experiments.safety: Max 60 psi, eye protection, remote pull-string release.

experiments.title: DIY spectroscope
experiments.summary: A card tube and a DVD grating reveal mercury lines in lamps and Fraunhofer lines in skylight. Python turns a phone photo into a calibrated spectrum.
experiments.safety: Aim at lamps or clouds, never at the Sun.

experiments.title: Cloud chamber
experiments.summary: Isopropyl alcohol and dry ice make a supersaturated layer where cosmic-ray muons leave trails, living proof of time dilation.
experiments.safety: Dry ice −78.5 °C and flammable alcohol: gloves, ventilation, no flames.

experiments.title: Moon & star trails
experiments.summary: Phone or camera on a tripod: stack Moon frames for √N less noise and star-trail arcs that measure the 23 h 56 m sidereal day.

experiments.title: First model rocket
experiments.summary: A balsa-fin kit on certified A/B/C motors. Prove stability first: Barrowman centre of pressure, measured CG, and the swing test.
experiments.safety: Certified commercial motors only, NAR Model Rocket Safety Code.

experiments.title: 3D-printed model rocket
experiments.summary: Parametric OpenSCAD: conical, ogive and von Kármán noses, BT-50/BT-60 fin cans, 18/24 mm motor mounts. Bambu print settings included.
experiments.safety: Certified motors; PETG/ASA near the motor; check stability.

experiments.title: Barometric altimeter payload
experiments.summary: Raspberry Pi Pico + BMP390 logging at 50 Hz. MicroPython detects launch, apogee and landing; tested on 40 synthetic flights.
experiments.safety: Passenger only: never connected to anything pyrotechnic.
